target_customer: High mix, low volume metal fabricators in aerospace, agriculture equipment and structural steel
problem: Programmed welding robots need weeks of setup and cause roughly 10% of parts to need rework. Forge wants a vision and AI system that maps parts and guides the arm automatically.
business_model: Modular autonomous factory units and robot intelligence system sold to manufacturers (pricing not public)
product_category: Robotic welding intelligence and modular factories

founders.name: Eoin Cobbe
education: Mechanical engineering degree, deferred to join YC, institution not named
previous_startups: Ran a manufacturing business (name not given)
founders.background_notes: Worked in steel fabrication and robotics per TechCentral, September 2025. Age stated as 21 in that article.

founders.name: Robert Cormican
founders.background_notes: Published researcher in AI and image quality (IEEE Open Journal of Vehicular Technology). YC page labels him Founder/CTO and CEO, so titles conflict. Education not stated.

competitors.name: Novarc Technologies
competitors.what: NovAI vision and cognition for cobot and robot welding; autonomous TIG system

competitors.name: Path Robotics
competitors.what: AI welding with Obsidian model, shown at FABTECH 2025

competitors.name: Hirebotics
competitors.what: Cobot welding with AI weld settings and seam tracking, shown at FABTECH 2025

technical_complexity.rationale: Sub millimeter 3D scanning, seam detection and closed loop robot control across welding, scanning and logistics are hard for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Path Robotics and Novarc already shipped similar vision guided welding. Forge had no disclosed deployments at the time.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found. Rivals kept shipping products in 2025 and 2026.

market_need_then: US manufacturers face a welder shortage and want automation for small batch work. Competitors launched AI welding products in 2025, showing active demand.

identity.voice_and_tone: Modular Autonomous Factories, built to scale; factories of the future

branding.community_and_virality: Irish press coverage (TechCentral, Irish Times, Portershed) of the Galway founders joining YC

brand_strength.rationale: Name is generic and shared with other Forge and ForgeOS companies, appears in search confusion. Brand coverage is mostly founder stories.

outcome_analysis: Forge Robotics is a very early YC Fall 2025 company with two young Irish founders and a $500K pre-seed tied to YC. One analysis reports zero disclosed customer deployments as of May 2026. The market is real but Path Robotics and Novarc are ahead, so the outcome depends on landing pilots and proving the 99% first-pass yield claim.
notes: One other profile says more than $700K (EUR 610K) including angels; unverified, not recorded as a round. Founder titles conflict between YC page and TechCentral. The $500K round is YC standard pre-seed reported by TechCentral. READY Robotics (ForgeOS) and Forge Automation are different companies.
